candidates.title: remove_stored (and rename_stored) report failure after the directory change is already done when the final parent-directory fsync fails, and the documented retry cannot complete: a resumed remove_stored throws ENOENT and no API re-syncs the parent
candidates.role: Honest operator (storing/removing stored machines, per the AUDIT.md table) -- in practice reached by the PRT stored player (support) and cartesi-machine CLI stored revert mode (support)
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp machine::remove_stored: remove files, os::remove_directory(dir), then os::sync_directory(parent); machine::rename_stored: os::rename_directory then os::sync_directory(to_parent/from_parent). Comment in remove_stored: 'Remove all files, the config file last, so an interrupted removal can be resumed without forcing'.
candidates.description: When the last step (fsync of the parent directory) fails, remove_stored throws although the directory is already gone; calling remove_stored again (the resume path the code comment promises) fails with 'unable to list directory ... No such file or directory', with or without REMOVE_FORCED, and there is no API that only syncs the parent directory, so the caller cannot make the removal durable or get a success. rename_stored behaves the same way: after the rename, a parent fsync failure throws, and a retry fails because the source no longer exists (sync_stored of the new name does re-sync its parent, so rename has a workaround).
candidates.trigger: Host fault: fsync(2) on the parent directory fails (EIO), injected in-process with an LD_PRELOAD shim on the first fsync during remove_stored.
candidates.reachability: Needs a failing fsync on a directory, which is a host fault. No adversary input reaches it. Does not change any hash or any directory O2 guarantees.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: section 8 lists 'Host faults, such as a full disk, as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state'. Here no hash or guaranteed directory is affected; the only effect is an error that cannot be cleared by retrying. So it is out of scope by that entry. If triage reads it as a persistence defect anyway: 2 Role: storing/removing machines is honest operator by the AUDIT.md table; the callers in this repository (prt.lua stored pair commit/revert, CLI) are support. 3 Medium case 'A persistence operation that fails loudly, without a wrong hash or damage to a directory that O2 guarantees, in an uncommon host setup that the manual documents, or while cleaning up after a stop' does not fit exactly (it needs a fault, not a documented host setup). 4 No rule is violated: R9 holds and O2 is untouched. 5 Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model' (the code comment's resume promise does not hold once the directory itself is gone).
candidates.threat_to_goal: None to the goal. A caller that treats the error as fatal (the PRT player asserts on errors) would stop and restart. On restart the directory is already gone and the player's fs.exists guard skips it, so the operator recovers. Only durability of the removal is left unconfirmed.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/DYNPERSIST/runfaults.sh (driver faultinj.lua, scenario 'remove', fault fsync #1, EIO) on an XFS reflink loop image: RESULT remove fsync 1 errno=5 error fired=true problems=1 :: resuming removal without forcing failed: unable to list directory '.../g1': No such file or directory. All other 167 injected runs reported an error with every invariant intact, or succeeded silently (msync MS_ASYNC in the destructor; ioctl FICLONE EOPNOTSUPP and linkat EPERM fell back to copy) with every invariant intact.
candidates.test_idea: Under an LD_PRELOAD shim that fails the first fsync after arming: store and sync a machine at dir D, arm, call cartesi.machine:remove_stored(D) and expect an error, disarm, then require that a second remove_stored(D) (or a documented sync call) succeeds, or that the first call succeeds once the directory is gone. Today the second call throws ENOENT (the test exits 1).

not_covered: JSON-RPC server-side fault injection: the shim only armed in the Lua client process, so faults inside cartesi-jsonrpc-machine during remote store/load/clone/sync/destroy/shutdown were not injected. Remote ops were covered only by the random sequences (fuzz.lua, about 30% of machines remote, including shutdown_server with shared machines and fork_server).
Allocation failures (operator new/malloc) were not injected. Earlier rounds covered them (R1-O2-3, R3-VARDIRTY-1).
Real crash/power-loss consistency (dm-log-writes, kill -9 mid-store, page-cache loss after an fsync error) was not tested. O2 excludes it, and R5-INVSTORE-1 covers fsync-error semantics.

Linux guests and large machines: only a 4 MiB bare-metal scribbling guest (random stores across 768 pages, automatic and manual yields, deliveries mixed into its PRNG) with phtc_size 1024 was used. Behavior when the page hash-tree cache evicts heavily on a large RAM, and flash drives and NVRAM ranges, were not fuzzed.

replace_memory_range and SHARING_CONFIG with mixed per-range shared flags were not part of the random model. I checked by hand that SHARING_CONFIG with only RAM shared leaves a spliced state after destroy+sync (shared RAM from the end of the session, unshared registers from the start) whose cached and rebuilt roots agree. That is the documented 'config' semantics, so it is not reported (see R3-VARCACHE-1 for the replace_memory_range splice).

The forked-pair revert pattern of prt.lua (shutdown, swap, rebind_server) and the stored-pair commit/revert sequence were not exercised literally; their building blocks (fork, shutdown, destroy, sync, clone, remove, load SHARING_ALL) were.
The PRT player restart runner and the CLI --revert-mode=stored were not run.
Windows/macOS persistence paths, btrfs, and ENOSPC from page faults on MAP_SHARED sparse or reflinked files (SIGBUS) were not covered.
Fault injection sampled only 4 to 5 call indices per (scenario, call kind) and skipped open/close/pread/lseek faults, because the 4-CPU host was at load average around 24.
runs: fuzz.lua random-sequence persistence fuzzer: 10 seeds x 300 steps = 3000 operations (XFS reflink loop image: seeds 1-6; plain ext4: seeds 101-103; seed 2 also run twice while the model was being fixed). Mix: create (local/JSON-RPC, optionally SHARING_ALL into a directory), run with deliveries (send_cmio_response or log_send_cmio_response), run_uarch/log_step_uarch/reset_uarch/log_reset_uarch, collect_mcycle/uarch_cycle_root_hashes, write_memory, clear_hash_tree, get_root_hash/get_proof, store (all/config/none), sync_stored, clone_stored, load (none/config/all, with and without clear_hash_tree), destroy, shutdown_server, fork_server, rename_stored, remove_stored. Oracles: every directory loads to its recorded root, with and without clear_hash_tree, with sampled node hashes equal to the live machine's at store/destroy; the live root equals a from-scratch content hash (store, then load with clear_hash_tree); verify_hash_tree holds; cached root equals rebuilt root for every directory. After fixing two model errors (store with none/config is documented to copy the initial state; locks refuse a shared load of a privately mapped directory), all runs had 0 failures. Fault injection: faultinj.lua + shim/faultshim.so on XFS, 12 scenarios, 168 injected runs (store_all/none/shared, clone, sync, load shared +/- clear, load none, destroy_shared, create_shared, rename, remove; faults pwrite/ftruncate (EIO, ENOSPC), fsync, mmap, flock, ioctl FICLONE (EIO, EOPNOTSUPP), linkat (EIO, EPERM), mkdir, rmdir, unlink, msync). One harness-level problem (above); no wrong hash and no damaged guaranteed directory. Also: concurrency.update_hash_tree 1 vs 4 on a shared directory gave identical roots, and a shared load with clear_hash_tree followed by an immediate destroy+sync reloads correctly.
